sections.heading: V1 Release Readiness and Meta Issue Status
sections.summary: Amsterdam chain upgrade unblocked many items; remaining should-fix-before-V1 issues are not blocking but Chase is not ready to cut a release yet.
sections.body:
- Chase merged a large batch of PRs last week and closed out many items on the meta issue, but discovered additional issues during the Amsterdam chain upgrade.
- None of the newly discovered issues are considered blocking, but some are still open under the "should fix before V1" category.
- The Amsterdam chain upgrade is now complete, which unblocked significant progress.
- Hive test pass percentages did not change much; Erigon has one open PR causing a test failure.
- Decision: no V1 release cut yet, but remaining open items will not block a future release.

sections.heading: Issue 915: eth_simulate State Override Edge Case
sections.summary: State overrides that create empty accounts produce states impossible on-chain; Felix has been asked to review this niche but complicated problem.
sections.body:
- [Issue 915](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/915) involves eth_simulate and eth_call state overrides that can make an account empty, asking clients to simulate a state that cannot exist on-chain.
- Chase considers this a niche problem and not a blocker for a V1 release.
- Felix has agreed to look at the issue; Łukasz has also reviewed it.
- Most remaining should-fix-before-V1 items are pending client team PR merges rather than spec disagreements.

sections.heading: Trace Namespace Spec and Geth Support
sections.summary: Geth is the only client not supporting the Trace namespace; lightclient committed to reviewing the 4,000-line go-ethereum PR today.
sections.body:
- [Issue 890](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890) and [PR 895](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/895) cover the Trace namespace spec.
- Banteg has done extensive work aligning the spec with every client except Geth; all other clients that engaged are in alignment.
- The execution-APIs spec PR is based on Banteg's go-ethereum PR (35791), so progress is blocked on the Geth team reviewing and merging that PR.
- lightclient confirmed he will look at it today but noted it is ~4,000 lines of code, so full review will take time.
- Łukasz raised process concerns about the dependency on Geth for spec progression; Chase acknowledged the concern but said removing Geth from the process is not realistic.

sections.heading: Opcode Tracer Storage Revert Behavior (PR 947 / Issue 949)
sections.summary: Post-Amsterdam opcode tracer differences found in storage revert output; Geth already merged a fix, Erigon and Reth have PRs open.
sections.body:
- [PR 947](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/947) fixes [issue 949](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/949), clarifying what happens to storage output when a transaction is reverted in the opcode tracer.
- Geth has already merged the fix; Nethermind and Besu already conform; Erigon and Reth have open PRs.
- Chase asked for spec verbiage review and approval; once remaining client PRs are merged, the spec PR can be merged.

sections.heading: Schema and Documentation PRs (941, 940, 942, 918, 943)
sections.summary: Several small schema and doc PRs were reviewed and approved; 941 to be merged, 940 to be reviewed shortly.
sections.body:
- [PR 941](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/941) and [PR 940](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/940) are small schema changes; Chase approved 941 and said he would merge it, and will review 940.
- [PR 918](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/918) updates examples to use `input` instead of the deprecated `data` property in the generic transaction schema, related to earlier discussion in issue 663.
  - Agreement that old property names should not appear in examples.
- [PR 943](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/943) fixes broken links in documentation; approved.
- [PR 942](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/942) (account overrides without storage) was grouped with these as another small schema change.

sections.heading: New Client Listing Policy (Ethlambda / PR 922)
sections.summary: Decision on adding Ethlambda to the spec deferred pending confirmation from Will Corcoran on whether the client will appear in the Glamsterdam blog post.
sections.body:
- [PR 922](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/922) proposes adding Ethlambda (`LA`) to the spec's ClientCode list.
- Ethlambda primarily targets Lean Ethereum (post-quantum Ethereum initiative led by Justin Drake) but has recently started beacon chain work and appears on the network crawler as Amsterdam-ready.
- lightclient explained the historical heuristic: client listing in execution-APIs follows which clients appear in the official EF blog post announcing network upgrades.
  - The person likely writing the next blog post is Will Corcoran.
- Decision: ask Will Corcoran whether Ethlambda will be listed in the Glamsterdam announcement before merging the PR.
  - If Ethlambda is on the blog post, merge; otherwise, hold off.
- ethrex (a different client) was noted as being on the Hoodi announcement but is not the client in question here.
- Lean Ethereum devnets are closed and run by Ethlambda using EF infrastructure.

sections.heading: eth_getLogs V2 Proposal (PR 900)
sections.summary: Boma plans to present PR 900 at ACDE; Łukasz urged aligning any new log endpoint with the Trustless Log Index EIP instead.
sections.body:
- [PR 900](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/900) proposes an eth_getLogsV2 endpoint.
- Boma intends to bring this PR to ACDE for broader discussion and decision.
- Łukasz expressed strong reluctance to add new endpoints that are not compatible with the Trustless Log Index EIP, arguing new work should prioritize trustless compatibility.
  - He suggested the proposal could potentially be combined with or aligned to the Trustless Log Index approach.
- lightclient clarified Łukasz's position: the trustless log index should be the preferred direction rather than adding more non-trustless endpoints.
- Boma acknowledged the feedback and asked if changes are needed before the ACDE presentation; no specific changes were requested beyond the trustless alignment concern.
